text: no rule given on referral chains

comments.text: The Data model explicitly defers the referral rule — "referredBy points at another Member (a member may be referred by at most one member; no rule given on referral chains)" — yet Open Questions asserts "the request settled the data model and its rules in full." These contradict each other. Two concrete cases are unsettled and worth one line each: can a member be their own referrer (referredBy pointing at the same row), and can referral cycles form (A refers B, B refers A)? If the answer is 'no rule needed, the platform's referential integrity is enough', say so here and the contradiction disappears; if cycles or self-referral must be prevented, that is a rule the bean table or a requirement must carry.

text: the balance is a field here; the movements that change it are not

comments.text: The Scope says "the balance is a field here; the movements that change it are not" — but nothing states whether pointsBalance is directly editable on the register's edit form. Under the declared default authorization ("any signed-in user, the platform default"), an editable balance means any signed-in user can set an arbitrary points value that the out-of-scope movements process is supposed to own. State the intent: either the balance is maintained only by the movements process (read-only here, or edited only by a role that owns adjustments), or staff may correct it manually on the register. As written, the spec's own scope argument cuts against silent free editing.

text: create, browse, search, edit and close out member records

comments.text: Scope lists "close out member records" as a distinct operation alongside create/browse/search/edit, but nothing defines what close-out does beyond the status lifecycle's value. Is closing just setting status to a closed value through the normal edit form, or does it have consequences the spec should state — e.g. can a closed member still be edited, issued cards, or serve as a referredBy target? One clause here (or a note on the status field) makes the operation testable; otherwise 'close out' is a word with no behaviour behind it.
